prompt: People in many countries now depend heavily on their smartphones. Why has this happened? What effects does this dependence have on individuals and on society?
essay:
The smartphone is usually described as addictive, which places the failure squarely inside the user. The more accurate account is that it became compulsory. Two developments turned an optional device into something close to a requirement for ordinary life, and the effects that follow are consequences of that compulsion rather than of anybody's weak self-control.

The first was consolidation. The phone did not defeat the camera, the map, the diary and the bank card in separate contests; it absorbed them, so abandoning it now means abandoning all of them at once. Prices fell throughout, and networks improved to the point where the device worked everywhere, which removed the last reason anyone had to keep a substitute.

The second was institutional. Once most people carried one, organisations began to assume everyone did. Banks made the phone the second factor in proving identity, employers started issuing shifts through applications, airlines retired the printed boarding pass. Each decision was individually reasonable and collectively coercive: the technology stopped being something a person chose and became a condition of access to services they cannot opt out of.

That distinction explains the effects. At the individual level the familiar cost is attention — a device designed to be checked is checked, and the capacity for uninterrupted thought erodes without anyone ever deciding to give it up. At the level of society the cost is sharper and much less discussed. Where a service exists only through a phone, the people least able to use one are shut out of it, and a handful of firms controlling the operating systems acquire a say in who reaches a bank or a hospital appointment. A technology adopted by choice can be moderated by choice; infrastructure has to be governed, and this infrastructure was assembled long before anyone decided that was what it was.
title: Why smartphones became impossible to give up
